name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags low-contrast elements in real time, so designers see violations immediately—not after a merge or a user complaint. The trade-off is a small performance hit during active design tweaks, but it prevents costly fixes later and keeps the interface accessible by default.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt chimes—if every tweak spams alerts, they’ll mute the tool or dismiss violations as noise. Instead, ship a pre-commit hook that blocks merges with low-contrast elements, forcing fixes before they reach users; the trade-off is slower iteration for designers, but it guarantees no bad contrast ships. Settle it with a 2-week trial: measure designer complaints vs. post-merge contrast fixes in production.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-commit hook that blocks merges with WCAG AA contrast failures. It forces fixes at the last responsible moment—before code reaches main—so users never see low-contrast elements, and designers learn the cost of ignoring accessibility early. The trade-off is slower merges when violations exist, but that delay is cheaper than retrofitting contrast fixes after release.

name: Pane
text: The pre-commit hook blocks merges, but it risks slowing down designers who need rapid iteration—especially when they’re prototyping in the dark. A better alternative is a staged warning system: flag violations in the design tool itself, then require fixes before the file is marked "ready for review," not before merge. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers bypass the hook versus how often they ignore early warnings.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a staged contrast enforcement system—live warnings in the design tool first, then a pre-commit hook blocking merges with WCAG AA failures.

Result: Designers see violations immediately during iteration, then are forced to fix them before code reaches users. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
